sub-disjunctīvus , a, um, adj.,
I.subdisjunctive; said of two statements opposed to each other in such a way that neither of them may hold good (postclass.): “haec verba: ille aut ille, non solum disjunctiva sed etiam subdisjunctivae orationis sunt, etc.,” Dig. 50, 16, 124 : “conjunctiones,” Prisc. p. 1029 P.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
